source.title: Where Investment Goes
source.summary: Capital allocation, the riba prohibition, real estate misallocation, and the gap between Islamic finance theory and practice.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: Two countries with identical savings rates can have vastly different growth outcomes depending on how capital is allocated. The financial system channels savings into investment, and its efficiency determines growth. Capital misallocation reduces TFP in developing countries by 30 to 50 percent. Islamic economics prohibits interest, which should theoretically redirect capital: equity-based financing (mudaraba, musharaka) aligns incentives and directs capital toward productive uses rather than safe borrowers with mediocre projects. But Islamic banking in practice hasn't delivered this. Most Islamic banks use murabaha, which is economically similar to conventional lending. Genuine profit-loss sharing remains rare. Meanwhile, Muslim-majority economies suffer from massive real estate misallocation and underdeveloped equity markets. The principles are sound. The implementation gap is enormous.
